subject: g.analyse output includes incorrect number of days and dates

messages.author: 7e6c3a3cdeaf087d
messages.subject: g.analyse output includes incorrect number of days and dates
parts:
Dear Vincent and All-

 

First, I want to say thank you for creating such a fantastic program. It is wonderful to have a freely available package that we can all use to generate comparable data.

 

I am running GGIR on actigraph GT3X csv files and I am having a strange issue with output. I was hoping there may be a simple solution that I am not finding.  These accelerometry data were collected over two days in Kenya (6/23/2016-6/25/2016).

 

When I run the data through GGIR, I get some odd results. The output from g.analyse shows over 7 days (summary.meas_dur_dys = 7.96875) and starts on the wrong date (daysummary.calender_date = 11/14/13 - 11/22/13).  I looked at the metashort dataframe, and the date and timestamps are correct (showing data from 2016-06-23T03:45:00+0300 through 2016-06-25T18:44:55+0300). I am not sure how the date and time can be correct for the metashort dataframe but incorrect in the MVPA output.

 

Any help or insights anyone can be provide would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] g.analyse output includes incorrect number of days and dates
parts:
Thanks David,
Possible explanations may include:
Your csv-viewer, .eg. MS Excel, interprets the dates incorrectly, this
might happen when working with data collected in a different country
or timezone than your location.
Q1: Do you have the same problem for other files from the same study?
Q2: Did you try inspecting the csv report with a simple text editor?
If yes, are timestamps correct?

A file got mixed up in the wrong folder
Q3: Is the accelerometer filename in the report in line with what you expect?

Considering that you are analysing csv data generated by GT3X monitors
it might be that timestamps were stored in a format I did not account
for. At the moment there are four different timestamp formats the code
can automatically deal with.
Q4: Can you send me the top hundred lines of the original
accelerometer csv file?

A longer measurement duration as expected is possible if you forgot to
stop the measurement after the intended wear period.
Q5: Did you inspect the data whether there are also 7+ days of body movement?

Trying to answer these questions should hopefully give you more insight.
Best, Vincent
